passage:
A museum displayed an ancient shoe found in a dry cave. It was simple, made from natural materials, and shaped by use.
Students were fascinated by the wear marks. The guide explained that the marks could show how someone walked and what ground they crossed.
The shoe made the past personal. A foot had pressed into it day after day.
Unlike a crown or sword, the shoe belonged to ordinary movement.
Students realized that history is not only made by leaders. It is also made by feet walking to fields, markets, homes, and unknown destinations.
A worn shoe can make a forgotten person briefly visible.
